title: Theory into practice
abstract: 'Theory into Practice. Composition, Performance and the Listening Experience' is the second publication in the series 'Collected Writings of the Orpheus Institute'. The series comprises articles concerning the activities of the Orpheus Institute. The centrale theme of this book is the relationship between the reflections about and the relization of a musical composition. In his paper Words about Music, or Analysis versus Performance, Nicholas Cook states that words and music can never be aligned exactly with one another. He embarks on a quest for models of the relationship between analytical conception and performance that are more challenging than those in general currency. Peter Johnson's article Performance and the Listening Experience: Bach's 'Erbarme dich' shows that a performance is an element within the intentionality of the work itself. He looks for scientific methods capable of proving the artisticity of a performance. The composer Hans Zender, in his A Road Map for Orpheus?, states that a composer must be capable of questioning obvious basic principles (such as equal temperament) and finding creative solutions.

narrative:
Short impact summary

This open-access scholarly book has clear evidence of academic uptake and usage. It has been cited 29 times, placing it in the top 10% most-cited works in its field and year, and it has also recorded 719 downloads, indicating sustained reader interest beyond citation alone.

Full narrative

Theory into Practice, published by Leuven University Press in 2021, shows a compact but meaningful impact profile centered on scholarly circulation and sustained use. Its 29 OpenAlex citations place it in the top 10% most-cited works for its field and year, suggesting that the book has entered ongoing academic conversations rather than remaining a niche publication. The citation landscape is concentrated in music scholarship, especially musicology, musical analysis, and performance-related research, which fits the book’s central concern with the relation between reflection on music and its realization in practice.

The citing record also suggests breadth across adjacent disciplines. Most citing works are book chapters, followed by journal articles, with appearances in venues such as Musicae Scientiae and Psychology of Music. The concepts attached to citing works point to a strong emphasis on musicology and musical analysis, but also show overlap with music perception, education, performance studies, and related humanities and social science domains. This pattern indicates that the book is being used not only as a contribution to music theory and performance studies, but also as a reference point in wider discussions of listening, interpretation, and musical meaning.

Usage evidence reinforces that scholarly attention. The book recorded 719 downloads through OAPEN, with monthly activity distributed across the year rather than confined to a single spike. It is also available as an open-access book in OpenAIRE, which likely supports its visibility and accessibility. Together, these signals show a work that is being read and reused in ways that go beyond citation counts alone.

There are also limited but noteworthy signs of public and teaching-related reach. The record includes two Crossref-linked public mentions and one teaching-related YouTube discussion, alongside library holding evidence in WorldCat. The available evidence does not support a larger claims framework than this, but it does show that the book has moved into both academic and informal educational contexts. Overall, Theory into Practice has a solid and clearly documented footprint as a cited, downloaded, and intermittently discussed contribution to music scholarship.
